audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor may include rebate economics curtailed by enacted PBM reform
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; FY2025 pharmacy-benefit revenue was $457.732 million, 35.5% of $1,288.661 million total revenue
audit_findings.mechanism: Vendor rebates reduce cost of services and increase OE; carrying FY2025 OE forward would overstate the anchor and future growth if retained rebates must be passed through without replacement fees.
audit_findings.evidence: For example, on February 3, 2026, the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2026 was signed into law and includes PBM reforms that would, among other things, require PBMs to disclose information on their costs, fees and rebates; require 100% of the rebates to be passed on to consumers; and impose other disclosure, reporting and audit requirements on PBMs.
audit_findings.explanation: This is not a demonstrated measurement error because the record does not provide the law's effective dates, covered contracts, retained-rebate amount, or replacement pricing. It is nevertheless reasonably capable of materially changing value: an enacted law directly affects an undisclosed profit source within a business representing 35.5% of FY2025 revenue, while the valuation capitalizes only $34.4 million of anchor OE.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the statutory effective dates and implementing guidance, map covered Progyny Rx contracts, quantify FY2025 retained rebates included in OE, identify replacement fees realized in 2026, and rerun all scenarios using normalized post-reform OE.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 contains transition activity from a client that did not renew
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the former client represented approximately $140.1 million of FY2024 revenue based on its filed 12% share, but the smaller 2025 transition cohort was not quantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Profit and working-capital cash flow from a finite transition agreement may be embedded in the $34.4 million OE anchor even though the agreement ended June 30, 2025.
audit_findings.evidence: Includes ART cycles performed in the first half of 2025 under the extended transition of care agreement with the large client who did not renew its service agreement.
audit_findings.explanation: The inclusion of transition activity is demonstrated, but an OE overstatement is not. The transition covered only qualifying members, and its revenue, gross profit and cash contribution are undisclosed. Evidence of replacement is encouraging but not conclusive: H1 2026, after the transition ended, exceeded H1 2025 revenue by $22.1 million and gross profit by $17.6 million. The record therefore cannot establish whether any residual anchor normalization would be material.
audit_findings.action: Isolate the transition agreement's 2025 revenue, gross profit, claims accruals and working-capital cash flows; calculate its OE contribution; reconcile that amount against continuing-client results through H2 2026; then rerun the anchor if it was not fully replaced.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized SBC may escape both the expense numerator and the capex deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.8 million, equal to 8.1% of the $34.4 million anchor; full removal would mechanically reduce base operating PV by about $39.3 million and base value by about $0.40 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: If capitalized SBC was excluded from operating expense, omitted from cash capex and later added back through depreciation, OE is overstated by the omitted economic compensation cost.
audit_findings.evidence: During the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, the Company capitalized $ 2.8 million, $ 1.4 million, and $ 0.6 million, respectively, in stock-based compensation related to the development of internal-use software.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the amount escaped deduction is unresolved, but its filed ceiling permits a scale test. Even charging the entire $2.8 million against recurring OE would reduce base value from $7.24 to approximately $6.84 per share, still far below the $25.94 market price and therefore not capable by itself of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the 2025 OE capex and SBC adjustments to total capitalized-software additions; confirm the $2.8 million was charged exactly once, and if omitted rerun all scenarios with a $2.8 million anchor reduction.

audit_findings.title: A large portion of the anchor depends on subjective year-end claims estimates
audit_findings.magnitude: $54.9 million accrued receivable less $30.0 million accrued claims payable, a $24.9 million net estimated gross-profit spread equal to 72.4% of the $34.4 million OE anchor; actual misstatement unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: True-ups change revenue, cost of services, gross profit, working capital and therefore OE; favorable and unfavorable revisions move value in opposite directions.
audit_findings.evidence: Auditing the Company’s estimates of accrued receivables and the related accrued claims payable was complex and required significant judgment as the estimates were sensitive to changes in the significant assumptions, including management’s assumptions regarding the lag between authorization date and service date, service changes and cancellations.
audit_findings.explanation: No error is demonstrated. The company states that historical adjustments were not material, and H1 2026 continued to state that original-estimate adjustments had not been material. Nevertheless, the $24.9 million net estimated spread is large relative to anchor OE, while the filings do not disclose subsequent settlement accuracy for the FY2025 cohort. The record cannot establish the direction or materiality of any remaining true-up.
audit_findings.action: Obtain subsequent-billing and claims-payment triangles for the December 2025 accruals, including cancellations and service changes; compare estimated versus realized revenue, claims and gross margin; rerun the anchor for the actual true-up and a supported downside case.

audit_findings.title: A nonrecurring retention-credit refund remains in the latest-year anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.1 million pretax, equal to 6.1% of the $34.4 million anchor; full removal would mechanically reduce base operating PV by about $29.5 million and base value by about $0.30 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The one-time G&A benefit increases FY2025 earnings and OE but should not be capitalized as recurring operating earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Other related general and administrative expense also included a benefit of $2.1 million in the year ended December 31, 2025 related to employee retention credit refunds.
audit_findings.explanation: The refund is a demonstrated nonrecurring benefit. Even conservatively removing the full pretax amount from recurring OE would reduce base value from $7.24 to approximately $6.94 per share, still far below the $25.94 market price; it therefore does not change the valuation conclusion by itself.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the OE schedule already removed the refund; if not, deduct the properly tax-adjusted $2.1 million benefit from the anchor and rerun the scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The dilution ceiling combines equity-award inventory and basic shares from different dates
audit_findings.magnitude: 99.497615 million valuation shares exceed 76.726798 million July 31, 2026 outstanding shares by 22.770817 million; even removing that entire increment would produce values of approximately $8.42, $9.38 and $10.52 per share for bear, base and bull
audit_findings.mechanism: Double-counted vested or exercised awards overstate the denominator and understate per-share value, while omitted new grants understate the denominator and overstate per-share value.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, as of December 31, 2025, there were an aggregate of 18,984,966 and 3,778,964 shares of our common stock subject to outstanding options and unvested restricted stock units, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The date mismatch is demonstrated, but the net denominator error is unquantified without an award rollforward. A decisive scale comparison is available: deleting the entire 22.770817 million increment—far more favorable than a proper dilution calculation—would leave even bull value at approximately $10.52 per share, still 59% below the $25.94 market price. The mismatch therefore cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 30, 2026 option, RSU, PSU and ESPP rollforward; reconcile exercises, vesting, net settlements, forfeitures, cancellations, new grants and repurchases to the later basic count; then rerun per-share values using one consistently dated fully diluted denominator.
